## Batch105 — HTTP MCP lifecycle retries and generation-safe session recovery (pre-edit)

Codex pin unchanged/clean. Re-read applicable development instructions and goal; batch104
is verified progress, not overall completion. No teach.md or Codex edits authorized here.

Source: rmcp-client/src/rmcp_client.rs:1316–1532 captures the exact RunningService for
an operation. Only typed SessionExpired404 triggers a serialized recovery. Under the
recovery semaphore, a different current Arc means another caller already recovered;
otherwise construct a fresh pending transport from the saved recipe, complete a fresh
handshake, then publish Ready only if not Closed. Retry the original operation once on
the recovered service; a second404 propagates, not recursive recovery. Each operation
phase has its own timeout; recovery uses the saved initialization timeout. Old service
references survive in-flight work. http_client_adapter.rs:148–278 classifies POST404
using the request's captured session presence before reading the body, not a mutable
current-session field. Bare404, auth401, generic500/network failures are not this signal.

Source streamable_http_retry.rs:22–249 supplies two 250/1000ms delays, three attempts,
one deadline across attempts/backoff. HTTP handshake retries transient transport/status
errors in initialize/discover or initialized notification by rebuilding the transport;
schema/JSON/auth/session errors are excluded. tools/list alone gets transient operation
retries, not tools/call/resources/prompts. Transient statuses are 408/429/500/502/503/504.
rmcp-client/tests/streamable_http_recovery.rs:111–280,400–453 tests initialization and
notification retry, tools/list retry, recovery with an initialization failure, double404
bounded recovery and non-session tool errors without replay. These Rust tests are read,
not run; no local Rust toolchain evidence is being substituted.

Corki currently performs one initialize and one notification, with no handshake retry;
MCPClient.request gives each exchange a timeout but no lifecycle retry. HttpMCPClient
has a single mutable session/helper/client; _post uses current session presence after
await, not the sent header snapshot. Manager -> connection lease -> client calls are
already the production route; physical-owner reconciliation is separate from session
expiry. B05/E01 **missing/partial**, P1: transient discovery can hide a healthy server;
expired sessions never recover; a naive header reset would violate concurrent ownership.

Plan: an HTTP-owned recovery coordinator with exact generation leases, serialized fresh
handshake/publish, independent bounded retry phases and owned cleanup. Capture original
static authentication/header recipe; create fresh per-generation HTTP client/helper,
never mutate an old admitted generation or silently relist/replace its catalog. Scope
transport retries narrowly, preserve cancellation, reject late publication after close,
and release retired generations after users finish. Runtime/native/compatible/CodeMode,
ledger/cold replay, concurrent404, failed/repeated recovery, cancellation/close and
header-first/body ownership require RED/GREEN evidence. Full OAuth, modern discovery,
SSE/remote/Windows and other A–E gaps are not closed by this stage.

### Implementation and regression evidence

Added mcp/http_recovery.py rather than growing another recovery loop in Runtime/Manager.
HttpMCPClient's production start/request path delegates to it; individual sessions retain
their own HTTPX client, protocol/session values and helper. Fresh sessions copy the original
resolved static header/bearer/cwd recipe. HTTP initialization and tools/list transient
retry use 250/1000ms delays under a shared phase deadline; fresh handshake is required
after initialize or initialized-notification failure. Ordinary tool/resource/prompt
operations have no generic transient replay. Session404 recovery compares failed/current
object identity under a lock, publishes only a complete handshake, and retries once outside
the recovery catch. Params are copied before awaiting, and existing policy timeout binding
is transferred to the selected generation. Recovery retains the original startup budget.

Generation leases retain old calls through completion; retirement closes only unused
generations, and late responses cannot overwrite the new generation's session. Root
shutdown closes admission, cancels/joins owned operations and joins all generation cleanup.
An injected HTTP carrier is explicitly borrowed by each HTTPX session and closed once by
the outer owner, after all generations; default HTTP sessions have separate clients/pools.

user-configured mcp-session-id header is not that authority. Classification and body skipping
use the captured value; neither later mutable session state nor remote response metadata can
manufacture it. Existing response-close ownership still joins cleanup before recovery.

### Batch106 implementation and final evidence

Added `src/corki/mcp/sse.py`: byte-incremental CR/LF/CRLF parsing, initial BOM,
one optional ASCII space after colon, multiline data, known fields, duplicate-field
checks, NUL-containing id filtering and bounded u64 retry parsing. An empty line
commits an event; EOF never flushes an unfinished line/event. Comments do not build
up retained event state. The existing Corki 16MiB defensive budget now applies to
the unfinished SSE event/line, not the accumulated response stream. JSON/non2xx body
limits remain separate. This is not exact legacy numeric-limit parity: Codex's local

`http_response.py::buffered_request` consumes successful request POST SSE incrementally,
selects a completed response/error matching the outgoing ID, stores it in a host-only
response extension and returns without waiting for peer EOF. It retains the batch103

handling. `client.py::_decode_http_response` consumes that host extension; its buffered
compatibility path uses the same parser. Control event types, malformed JSON and inbound
server requests cannot masquerade as a tool completion. EOF without a final response
is a protocol failure. A read transport failure after successful POST response headers
becomes safe MCPProtocolError, not the HTTP send-error category used by batch105's
initialization/tools-list retry. It cannot cause automatic POST replay.

### Batch107 implementation and focused evidence

Added `mcp/sse_resume.py`, wired directly from `http_response.py::buffered_request`
for successful ordinary request POST SSE, excluding initialize. It captures the sent
request headers/URI and request identity, strips POST body headers, and updates only
completed SSE cursor/retry fields. Each replacement carrier starts a fresh parser;
an incomplete previous line/event cannot contaminate the replay. Control/invalid-JSON
events may still supply a valid cursor. Empty cursors remain distinct from absent ones.
GET uses the same endpoint, optional session/auth/protocol headers and Last-Event-ID,
with no body or redirects. As in the Codex adapter, GET application/json MIME is also
accepted as an SSE byte stream, not decoded as an ordinary JSON result.

EOF consumes a stored server interval, otherwise 1s. Transport/parser failure with a
cursor resumes immediately. Failed connection attempts use 2s/4s/... delays maxed with
an unconsumed server interval; successful GET starts a new attempt sequence. There is
no new retry-count limit, and existing MCP request/operation deadlines and cancellation
bound the entire continuation. The exponent saturates at63 to avoid Python overflow on
unreachable enormous attempt counts; this is not a claim of emulating Rust u32 overflow.
GET rejection/status/auth/404 and send failure stay in this continuation loop, never
ordinary POST session-recovery or lifecycle-send retry. Event-size violation has a
dedicated SseEventTooLarge subtype and is always terminal, even with a prior cursor.

Moved the existing owned-response carrier and primary-error-preserving close protocol
to `mcp/http_stream.py`; ordinary buffered and resumed responses share it. A carrier
closes before another GET is acquired or a delay begins. No unowned reconnect/background
task was introduced; request/generation lease and shutdown remain owned by HttpRecovery.
Further fault injection exposed that a resumed response's close-time httpx.ReadError
could leak into tools/list POST retry. The accepted-SSE boundary now converts remaining
HTTP errors, including close failures, into safe MCPProtocolError; cancellation is not
caught by that conversion. No database/schema/history fields changed.

New `tests/unit/mcp/test_sse_resume.py`: **45** cases covering stateless/stateful GET,
empty/nonempty cursors, EOF/read error, no-ID/unfinished-ID/NUL-ID refusal, cursor updates
before event filtering, per-carrier parser reset/BOM, initialize exclusion, exact delay
traces and GET status/send failures, GET JSON MIME, parse-error resumption, fatal size
limits, auth/404/405/503/redirect/content-type failure under the same deadline for both
tools/list and tools/call, delay/send/read/close repeated cancellation, close failure
classification, concurrent request cursor/header isolation, client shutdown and actual
local HTTP/1 chunked POST -> GET with no POST replay and no final GET EOF requirement.

They assert one remote POST, one GET, next-model Observation, exactly one host completion
and ledger row, all carrier closures, and cold history/ledger stability without replay.
Scripted models prove the Harness paths, not real model selection. Total new cases **54**.

### Batch108 implementation and evidence

New `mcp/initialization.py::validate_initialization` validates the required initialization
result and every known nested capability/implementation/icon field described above.
It returns only the typed protocol/instructions fields the current client consumes;
remote metadata does not become execution authority. No arbitrary version whitelist,
URL/icon fetch, additional nonempty-string check or unknown-field prohibition was added.
MCPClient.initialize calls it before marking protocol readiness/sending initialized;
JSON and stdio requests share initialization envelope validation and ID/error handling.
ID-less JSON error responses preserve the server error, instead of becoming ID mismatch.
The validation also runs inside batch105 replacement handshakes; invalid replacements
are closed and never published or used to replay the rejected original tool call.

`initialization_event` implements the HTTP initialization-specific SSE first-Response
selection, independent of event name and ordinary malformed-JSON skip rules. Empty data
uses the same Rust whitespace set; valid error/notification/request messages are skipped
at this HTTP transport stage. The first response, including a conflicting ID, reaches
service validation. Ordinary tool SSE/GET semantics from batch107 remain unchanged.
Successful initialization HTTP replies require supported MIME. Initialized notifications
accept202/204 without reading a body or a valid JSON-RPC JSON body; SSE/untyped payloads
fail and still join owned close. This is not full request/notification typed serde.

line codec. Locked rmcp async_rw.rs:128–190 strips blank lines, skips JSON syntax/EOF
errors, sends id-less Invalid Request for typed data errors and continues waiting.

behavior, strips BOM, and uses its handshake future to route the first valid response

Invalid Request and do not falsely complete initialization. Reply writes share the
existing stdin lock, and readers retain a future/list/pipe/lock rather than the client,
preserving existing weak-owner/GC cleanup behavior. The earliest draft/test incorrectly
made stdio syntax errors fatal; that draft was corrected against this source before

### Batch109 implementation and validation

`http_routing.py::HttpResponseRouter` registers pending futures before POST, distinguishes
send completion from RPC completion and routes JSON/SSE responses across request and ordinary
notification POSTs plus common GET. Sending tasks are generation-owned: a response arriving
before POST completion does not cancel/replay that POST, and close still joins it. Caller
cancellation cancels/joins its own send without cancelling the common receiver or another
call. Numeric IDs remain generation-scoped, including reused ID2 across a404 replacement.
`HttpMCPClient::_initialize_session` starts common GET only after completed initialization
and only with negotiated session; failed handshake does not create a receiver. Existing
HttpRecovery leases retain old-generation receivers until their admitted calls release.
Router close joins sends/receiver before DELETE/helper/client close.

Common GET uses captured session/protocol/static+helper headers, explicit Accept, no body
or read timeout, no redirects; initial405 returns unsupported, other initial failures close
and log a safe exception type without failing the service. `sse_resume` reuses the incremental
parser and reconnect policy, but common streams continue after responses and reconnect even
with no completed ID. Request streams remain cursor-gated and now yield their first Response
regardless of which pending ID it resolves; a closed request stream fails its own unanswered
RPC. Unknown/duplicate/cancelled IDs do not complete any other request. Source service.rs:
1689–1722 confirms valid unmatched responses and id-less errors are dropped rather than
failing the current POST; matching is against the full pending pool. Invalid typed IDs
(bool/float/null result) still fail; full typed ordinary-message decoding remains open.

### Batch110 implementation and verification: incoming service / RPC cancellation

`mcp/inbound.py::InboundService` is now wired into ordinary HTTP JSON, request SSE,
common GET and real stdio receive paths. It separates server request IDs from the
outbound response map, echoes the exact string/signed-64-bit integer ID, replies to

for unimplemented requests. The initialization-specific receive path remains separate.

fields and use the reference severity groups; logging excludes envelope _meta.

### Follow-on pre-edit source audit: graceful inbound reply drain

Source `rmcp3.2.0/src/service.rs::serve_inner` uses the same generic loop for RoleClient
and RoleServer. Transport receive EOF selects QuitReason::Closed; service cancellation
selects QuitReason::Cancelled (1395–1438). It stops receiving new service events, then
joins already dispatched response sends and drains pending handler responses before
transport.close, with a shared5s/2s budget respectively (1725–1765). RunningService
owns a cancellation DropGuard; explicit close cancels and awaits the loop, while
Codex rmcp_client.rs holds Arc<RunningService> in its Ready state and in-flight
operations. Do not mistake last-reference drop for an awaited host close API.
The source `tests/test_inflight_response_drain.rs` was read fully: it verifies a
RoleServer slow response survives read-side EOF. It is relevant shared-loop evidence,
not an executed Rust test or a directly matching Codex client integration test.

Current Corki reproduction (terminal02a5c8): feed one valid server ping followed by
EOF into the real `_read_stdio` reader with its actual InboundService. Expected one
empty successful reply with the exact server ID; actual reply list is empty, with
zero tasks remaining. Buffered EOF lets reader.finally cancel the newly scheduled
reply before its coroutine runs. This is a deterministic lost-response defect,
not a task leak and not a flaky timeout. HTTP generation close has the corresponding
immediate inbound cancel/join policy; it still needs its own behavior reproduction.

Next repair acceptance must distinguish EOF, explicit shutdown and exceptional exit;
stop new inbound admission; preserve transport ownership until existing replies
complete or the reference drain deadline expires; join cleanup under repeated caller
cancellation; and avoid changing outbound tool retry/replay semantics. Cover queued
and active replies, exhausted drain budgets, concurrent close/EOF, real stdio and
HTTP control POST ordering. Current110 blocked-close test proves immediate cleanup
ownership and will need an explicit grace-deadline-aware expectation, not removal.
No production change for this follow-on has been made in batch110.

### Batch111 pre-edit audit: natural stdio EOF reply loss

Previous goal turn was progress:110 final gates/artifact evidence and corrected cache/
host-shutdown applicability. Full objective re-read; pinned Codex remains clean and

Scope for this repair: natural stdio EOF must stop admitting incoming requests and
drain already-owned replies for the reference5s budget before failing unresolved RPCs.
An explicit host close must still be able to interrupt that grace period and complete
its process cleanup; no new2s pre-termination policy is introduced. Ordinary HTTP GET
EOF is a reconnect event, not service EOF, and this repair must not close that service.

Current `_read_stdio` always calls immediate inbound.aclose in finally, dropping a
buffered ping directly followed by EOF. Required tests before edits: queued default
replies, a delayed active reply, deadline exhaustion, close/EOF races and repeated
cancellation; actual subprocess half-close must prove the wire reply arrives before
the server exits. Actual Runtime must retain successful prior tool Observation/ledger
without replay even when the same server half-closes after its tool result. Failure
and explicit shutdown paths must not accidentally acquire the natural-EOF grace.

Further wrapper tracing before finalizing111: LocalStdioTransport::close (87–98)
closes AsyncRw's write half, then waits3s for the child before kill. Thus drain alone
is insufficient: natural EOF must also close the write half and reap the owned child.
Locked async_rw.rs::receive maps an I/O read error to None, hence the service sees
Closed and uses the same5s drain; the earlier broad statement that all reader errors
should skip grace is corrected. Internal Python failure and explicit cancellation are
kept distinct. Extend tests to assert sink EOF/reaping after the reply and I/O-error
classification; HTTP reconnect and Codex explicit process-first shutdown stay separate.

Additional111 admission invariant: service.rs breaks its event loop before drain, so
new PeerSinkMessage requests/notifications cannot be dispatched to the transport during
that phase. Corki's independent direct `_write` path was still usable while the reader
drained, potentially sending new side effects to a server with no readable response
channel. Add notification and tool-call failure tests before fixing this gate. The
reverse-reply static sink remains writable during drain; only new outbound work is
rejected. This aligns the no-new-send invariant, not rmcp's exact delayed error timing.

### Batch111 implementation and staged evidence

`InboundService.aclose(grace_seconds=...)` now stops admission synchronously and owns
one shielded close task. Natural EOF gives existing replies a shared5s send budget;
expiry cancels and joins remaining replies, but the budget does not detach transport
cleanup. An explicit close interrupts grace, and repeated/concurrent close does not
re-cancel a reply already in its cleanup finally. Cancellation is propagated only
after owned close completes. Stdio is_closed includes this closed admission state;
ordinary `_write` checks it while holding the sink lock. Reverse replies use the
separate static sink and can still complete during graceful drain.

`_read_stdio` distinguishes natural EOF/legacy read I/O failure from internal exceptions
and local cancellation. Its finally drains inbound replies, then invokes pipe/process-
owned `_finish_stdio_eof`, then resolves remaining RPC futures with the close error,
including when the reader was cancelled during cleanup. EOF transport finish closes
stdin, waits3s for child exit, kills/reaps on expiry and closes owned pipe transports.
The reader/finish closures retain the process, not the client, preserving existing GC
ownership. Explicit host process termination and ordinary HTTP SSE resume remain
separate; no new2s pre-termination policy or HTTP service-EOF inference was introduced.

Previous goal turn was progress (112 implementation/full3392/installed2844). Full

Before adding another host input consumer, current Corki realtime input has an actual
ownership gap: `_consume_realtime_turn` spawns a read_message task but its cancellation
and finally clauses only join the output consumer. Cancelling the application while
both are pending can leave a terminal prompt alive to consume later input. A directly
awaited gather on prompt cancellation can also re-cancel its cleanup under repeated
caller cancellation. This is an A08/E cancellation defect and a prerequisite for safe
elicitation/steering input arbitration, not an implementation of elicitation itself.
Add tests with the actual LangGraphRuntime and a blocking UI read/cleanup; require the
reader and output consumer to be joined on cancel, normal completion and renderer
failure, preserving terminal errors and buffered-input behavior. Do not expand approval
or UI product scope in this ownership repair. Full elicitation still requires the
session host channel, authority/router, form/URL handling, all timeout layers and
Code Mode result gate; none is declared complete by this prerequisite.

repeated task cancellation. The existing completed-input retention path remains in
place. Prompt-task cleanup exceptions are logged by type without printing private
prompt data or replacing the primary renderer exception/cancellation.

shared by the Runtime's MCP manager before initialization and across generations;

manager-owned router before startup. Standard form/url (legacy missing-mode form)
requests enter independently owned reverse-RPC tasks. Missing host declines; invalid
envelope returns InvalidParams; host exceptions return InternalError with safe logs.
The router strips progressToken, allocates independent public tokens, isolates host
metadata, normalizes response content and removes pending requests on scope exit.
Counted per-logical-client ActiveTime is shared across HTTP replacement generations;
HTTPX's independent timeout is disabled only behind owned active-time request budgets.
Header helper accounting follows that active clock. HTTP retries retain a wall-clock
eligibility deadline without canceling a currently paused attempt; startup retains its
separate wall-clock budget. Code Mode exec/wait gate captured results on the manager's
session-wide router, not only the cell's own calls.

### Batch118 pre-edit audit: Turn-owned system timezone

Objective re-read; batch117 is verified progress. Codex remains clean at the pinned
commit; Corki has228 existing status entries, all retained. No118 edits preceded

Agent-reach Jina Reader was used to inspect the exact locked iana-time-zone0.1.65
primary source (Cargo.lock8584; expected archive checksum
e31bc9ad994ba00e440a8aa5c9ef0ec67d5cb5e5cb0cc7f8b744a35b389cc470; archive not downloaded
or checksum-verified, no Rust execution). Read sources:
[Linux](https://docs.rs/crate/iana-time-zone/0.1.65/source/src/tz_linux.rs),
[Darwin](https://docs.rs/crate/iana-time-zone/0.1.65/source/src/tz_darwin.rs),
[Windows](https://docs.rs/crate/iana-time-zone/0.1.65/source/src/tz_windows.rs).
Linux checks /etc/localtime recognized symlink prefixes, then /etc/timezone, then
OpenWrt config. Darwin resets CoreFoundation's cached system timezone and copies its
name. Windows uses Windows.Globalization.Calendar.GetTimeZone. These do not use TZ
as their system-name source. Corki currently derives timezone from astimezone's
offset/name every Step; that is both a source mismatch and missing Turn ownership.

Plan before production edits: implement system-name resolution with explicit Etc/UTC
failure fallback, store timezone in newly admitted CorkiState and reuse it for normal,
realtime and token-budget compaction builders. Old checkpoints without this field
capture a fresh name at their next prepare boundary; frozen prepared requests must
not be rewritten. Keep date refreshed, not frozen. Windows may use a bounded fixed
PowerShell query of the same WinRT API as an adapter, never interpolated model input;
test this adapter offline and distinguish it from actual Windows execution. Add real
Runtime RED tests, then source-mapped resolver and checkpoint/compaction tests.

Shell trace is also now concrete, not closed: session/session.rs1167–1194 selects a
Session shell; shell-command/src/shell_detect.rs reads the Unix passwd entry (not
SHELL), detects supported types, checks actual files/PATH and platform fallbacks.
core/shell.rs::derive_exec_args changes login flags, not shell identity. Direct
unified_exec.rs::get_command uses the Session shell unless a model shell *type*
override is resolved; Corki process.py currently switches login=false to /bin/sh
and separately rereads ambient SHELL. This requires joint discovery, prompt and real
execution changes, not a display-only rename. It remains the next production batch;
full A–E scope, other platform resolvers and all open audit rows remain active.

### Batch119 pre-edit audit: selected shell identity and direct execution

Objective re-read. Batch118 was verified progress. Codex clean at the pinned commit;
Corki232 preexisting status entries preserved. core/session/session.rs1167–1194 chooses
the Session shell; environment_selection.rs stores it and environment.rs renders its
typed name. shell-command/src/shell_detect.rs::default_user_shell reads Unix passwd,
not ambient SHELL; supported types resolve passwd-file→PATH→platform paths. Default
fallback order is user type then zsh/bash on macOS, bash/zsh on other Unix, PowerShell
on Windows, finally /bin/sh or cmd.exe. PowerShell tries pwsh then powershell.
core/shell.rs::derive_exec_args retains shell identity for either login setting;
PowerShell uses optional -NoProfile then -Command, cmd uses /c. Direct
tools/handlers/unified_exec.rs97–126 resolves model shell input as a *type*, not an
arbitrary executable path. allow_login_shell defaults true (config/mod.rs3746);
false makes omitted login false and rejects an explicit true before spawning.

Corki builder rereads ambient SHELL; ProcessManager does not own selected shell state,
and _spawn changes to /bin/sh for login=false. exec_command has no shell override or
allow-login gate. Batch118's real pipe/PTy probe already demonstrates this identity
mismatch. No shell production edits have preceded this saved difference.

Plan: a shared typed shell/discovery module, one immutable selection per ProcessManager
(Runtime Session), builder bound to the same name, typed argv for pipe and PTY without
changing process ownership. Add exec_command shell type override and tools.allow_login_shell
configuration; keep per-call overrides from mutating the Session default. Standalone
builders also capture a default instead of following later ambient SHELL changes.
Tests must cover actual Runtime direct/Code Mode calls, known/unknown/unavailable type
fallback, Unix/macOS/Windows discovery order fixtures, config errors and existing
cancel/startup/retention/output semantics. Model override paths must never execute an
arbitrary file merely because its basename names a recognized shell. Existing117
field-escaping tests should inject explicit snapshot names, not impersonate OS shell
discovery through SHELL. OS sandbox, elevated Windows policy, remote environments,
zsh-fork/shell snapshots and host overrides remain separate open branches, not waived.

authority by parsing their environment prompt text. Add a failing cold-reopen test
before this further production change.

No process startup/join/pruning/observation ownership was intentionally changed.

comment that SessionId always equals a root ThreadId is not sufficient for this path.

(number.rs499–525, de.rs899–921/1296–1303); no trailing bytes or whitespace are accepted.
NumberVisitor also accepts its single private map (number.rs444–456). Both raw map
end_map and buffered visit_content_map/end reject unconsumed extra keys
(de.rs1093+,serde private/de.rs1105–1115). Preserve raw/buffered/Value boundaries when
implementing this, rather than globally converting objects with any matching key.

Confirmed source chain: SSE responses.rs361/519 decodes both done and added through
from_value::<ResponseItem>. Enabled arbitrary_precision Number.deserialize_any first
tries u64/i64, then u128/i128; serde ContentVisitor has only64-bit numeric visitors,
and the core Visitor defaults1404/1466 reject128-bit values. TaggedContentVisitor
buffers all non-tag values (private/de.rs859–888), including ignored/unknown nested
fields. Thus certain integers invalidate the whole item, not the whole SSE stream;
generic envelope metadata/response Value and raw legacy item decoding are different.

Corki currently materializes every number but performs no Value-to-Content numeric
admission check. responses.py also appends unfinished function buffers to final
ModelCompleted after terminal, so simply skipping a bad done item would still allow
an earlier added item to execute. Codex turn.rs2496+ added handles previews/diff
consumers, while2384+ done drives actual tool dispatch; there is no equivalent
promotion of unfinished calls at Completed. Remove that unsafe fallback. Retain
Corki's explicitly compatible completed.output path, but subject its item candidates
to the same numeric check so a bad done cannot be resurrected from the terminal list.

Also trace private-map classification, because otherwise the same integer encoded as
{"$serde_json::private::Number":"..."} bypasses the intended boundary. serde Value
classifies only the first key (value/de.rs121–144); RawValue uses a nested JSON string.
Single-field and string validation plus full-number syntax are required. Typed raw
metadata Number accepts only the Number map, not the RawValue map; typed raw arguments/
tools are Value fields and must apply Value classification after Content buffering.
Ignored raw fields must not be globally reinterpreted. CLI additionally enables
serde_json/preserve_order via its nonoptional tui dependency (tui/Cargo.toml96), so
first-key order and duplicate last-value/first-position semantics are significant.

### Next recovery discrepancy — already-persisted pending input during TokenBudget reset

Read-only probe3a291f follows ContextWindowManager.prepare -> _reset_context with
a legacy/recovery pending user and bound skill already present in the raw journal.
prepare reports a valid three-item replacement, but cold active_history fails:
"compaction replacement is incomplete: expected 3 items, found 1".
_reset_context counts pending objects in replacement_item_count yet reuses their
existing storage IDs. SQLite append's intentional identical-item idempotence skips
those duplicates, so only the fresh context item is actually inserted after the
marker. This is a concrete C03/C04/A07/E recovery bug, not a grouping-test fixture
or an acceptable provider limitation. Ordinary summary compaction already creates
retained copies for persisted pending items; reset must obey the same append-only
identity invariant without reclassifying the input as a fresh memory source.

Native start_new_context_window atomically replaces the in-memory annotated history;
turn.rs pre-sampling context setup precedes fresh input recording, so its new window
is not implemented by counting duplicate journal IDs. Corki's SQLite/checkpoint
representation must preserve that observable window/input behavior. Next acceptance
requires an actual Runtime graph checkpoint before call_model, cold resume with the
original input/skill body exactly once, complete replacement records and unchanged
old archive. Test the existing-input and not-yet-stored cases separately and preserve
normal mid-turn reset semantics (old sampled input is not automatically resurrected).
No new production reset change yet;143's installed snapshot is still being verified.

### Batch149 before implementation — dedicated-memory filesystem error boundary

Native source re-traced: ext/memories/src/backend.rs3f2084 typed domain errors
versus Io; tools/mod.rs0ccbb8 maps only Io to FunctionCallError::Fatal; read.rs
57a58e calls the backend and preserves that mapping. core/tools/parallel.rs
handle_tool_call1b321a maps Fatal to CodexErr::Fatal, other failures to model output.
Local source fully read for this boundary: local.rs0c245c, local/read.rse055d0,
local/list.rs32b847, local/path.rs378d36, local/ad_hoc_note.rs526534; search.rs
d1ba06 covers all filesystem traversal/read error branches (remaining matcher code
is outside this error change). Initial missing/hidden path, invalid/non-file path,
bad bounds and duplicate note are semantic failures. Metadata/list/read/write I/O
is fatal; vanished directory/entry during enumeration is skipped, but disappearance
after validation when reading a file is fatal. Invalid UTF-8 is fatal for read,
deliberately skipped for search. A failed note write can leave partial bytes;
neither automatic retry nor falsely reporting successful creation is acceptable.

Corki memory/tools.py6d0c6b currently turns every OSError/UnicodeError/ValueError
into an Observation; backend.py6efbde reuses bare FileNotFoundError/FileExistsError
for both semantic and real I/O failures and rglob can suppress directory failures.
Tools executor015292 already propagates FatalToolError; graph3a0cb0 cancels/joins
parallel siblings and Runtime publishes a non-retryable tool failure. Nested Code
Mode dispatch intentionally converts Fatal to a rejected tool promise/Observation;
this existing separate boundary must be preserved rather than made universally fatal.

Plan: distinguish backend-generated missing/duplicate errors from operation-time
I/O while retaining their public builtin exception ancestry; use explicit lstat
and sorted non-following traversal so permission errors are not mistaken for missing
or empty results. Convert only real storage I/O/decoding failures to FatalToolError
at the dedicated tool boundary. Preserve semantic Observations, binary search skip,
cancel control flow, create-new note behavior, and no replay of uncertain writes.
Tests must enter actual runtime-owned memory tools, inspect persisted observations,
terminal and model sampling, inject operation-specific metadata/enumeration/read/
write failures, and cover semantic negatives, cancellation and parallel cleanup.
This closes an identified D/E boundary, not namespace/schema/cursor contracts or
the still-open complete phase-two instruction contract. No149 production edit yet.

Complete native tools/list.rs and search.rs re-read694fa1, schema.rs and note tool
1a17ce, tools/mod.rs0ccbb8, read.rs57a58e and backend.rs3f2084 establish:
- Canonical namespace memories with add_ad_hoc_note/list/read/search leaf names.
- List/search cursor is Option<String>, max_results is Option<usize>, default/max
  2000/200; handler clamps zero to1 and above-max to max. Optional explicit null
  is accepted by serde Option even when the advertised input schema omits null.
- Search match_mode is an internally tagged object: {type:any}, {type:all_on_same_line},
  or {type:all_within_lines,line_count:usize}; not Corki's string plus within_lines.
- Read accepts only path/line_offset/max_lines, with fixed default20000-token backend
  budget. It does not expose Corki's extra max_tokens argument.
- List entries use entry_type, cursors return strings, note success is {}, and
  JsonToolOutput returns an actual JSON value in Code Mode (5f7816), not a string.
- Input objects deny unknown fields; parse_args accepts whitespace-only function
  arguments as {}. Input schema hints are not synonymous with serde validation:
  e.g. min1 hints versus clamp0 and optional null, and note schema's leading-letter/
  digit slug hint versus backend's all-lowercase/digit/hyphen validation.

### Batch157 implementation and regression evidence

bind_model_settings now binds _admitted_model_info as an exact-model-only view and
leaves the host catalog unchanged. Other exact/prefix/scoped queries still resolve
through that catalog. ModelContextInfo.used_fallback_model_metadata is True for
synthesized metadata, False after actual catalog resolution, and None when provenance
was not recorded (old snapshots or unresolved host metadata). The internal exact view
retains that value across cold recovery; arbitrary catalog entry markers do not
override actual lookup provenance. Existing window/tool overrides remain baked into
the admitted snapshot. Runtime captures its warning owner before yielding Started;
future-default updates cannot retarget an old paused observer's fallback warning.

Additional concrete156 defect found by the new serializer tests97a93f: JsonPlus
encodes tuple fields as msgpack arrays, reconstructs lists, and catches constructor
exceptions by returning None (actual dependency source808c27). Strict tuple checks
in ModelContextInfo therefore erased that object and its parent snapshot.156 tests
with a duplicate business-ledger snapshot masked the checkpoint failure.157 re-freezes
only the finite sequence fields before validating; actual checkpoint-only Runtime
recovery now proves the snapshot is retained without a ledger backup. Legacy-msgpack
encoding without the new provenance field restores None honestly. A present null/
invalid checkpoint model snapshot now fails admission; absence remains the legacy
fallback. This corrects156's overly broad checkpoint acceptance evidence.

### Batch164 prerequisite audit: active writer ownership before archive/recovery mutation

Archive trace c4095a/d078b2/052da9: app-server thread_processor.prepare_thread_for_removal

acquires lifecycle/live-writer/cross-process locks and rejects any remaining active recorder.
It moves owned rollouts with rollback if metadata update fails; unarchive participates in the
same cross-process lock, restores files, touches mtime and updates metadata. A metadata-only
archive switch without writer coordination would omit essential A/E lifecycle behavior.

Native local/live_writer.rs create_thread/resume_thread acquire WriterLockCoordinator before
creating or opening a live recorder, retain the guard in its lifetime, and reject a second owner.
writer_lock.rs uses OS file locks, not PID/age guesses: a coordination lock protects stale-lock
cleanup and release/remove, try_lock returns Conflict for a live same-thread writer, unrelated
thread writers are independent. writer_lock_tests.rs covers competing coordinators, release/
reacquisition and stale-vs-active cleanup. All these sources were read, not executed as Rust tests.

Corki Runtime has only per-instance asyncio locks; no cross-instance/process writer ownership
was found. _ensure_ready -> _initialize -> _ensure_thread permits a second Runtime for the same
persisted Thread. More immediately, SessionRepository._create_schema unconditionally changes
ALL running tool_executions to interrupted, even when another live Runtime owns a tool and the
new constructor belongs to a different Thread. Opening a repository is not evidence of process
death. claim_tool_call already refuses unknown outcomes without replay independently of that
mass update; removing unsafe constructor recovery must retain that no-replay guarantee.

164 portable locking reference checked against primary docs: Python's
[msvcrt.locking](https://docs.python.org/3/library/msvcrt.html) locks from current offset,
permits bytes beyond EOF, and LK_LOCK stops after10 retries. Microsoft's
[_locking](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/locking?view=msvc-170)
documents EACCES for contention and immediate LK_NBLCK. Use native POSIX flock or Windows
byte lock, without treating the CRT's fixed retry count as evidence an owner died. Windows
execution is not available in this macOS workspace and will not be claimed verified.

### Batch164 implementation and initial verification

Added storage/file_lock.py (POSIX flock / Windows CRT byte locks) and thread_writer.py.
Coordinator is scoped to the resolved canonical database; opaque Corki Thread IDs are hashed
for bounded safe lock names. A coordination file protects stale cleanup and close/unlink from
inode replacement races. Only matching owned lock names are cleaned; active kernel locks and
unrelated files survive. No TTL/PID liveness guessing or stale-owner auto-replay was added.
Async ThreadWriterLease joins an in-flight acquisition even after repeated cancellation and
closes a returned guard before propagating cancellation. Descriptors are non-inheritable via
Python os.open defaults; process death releases the kernel lock.

Runtime acquires ownership before its canonical Thread initialization, retains it between Turns,
rejects a competing owner before input/model work, releases on initialization failure for retry,
and releases after close joins Turn/control/tool/backend/checkpoint cleanup. _ensure_thread also
owns/rejects late creation and releases on create/identity failure. Failed control-shutdown is
recorded while remaining cleanup continues, rather than leaking the writer through an early exit.
SQLiteSessionRepository construction no longer mass-updates running tool ledgers. Existing
claim_tool_call still returns unknown-outcome/no-replay observation for unfinished entries, so
removing that constructor mutation does not authorize replay or falsely complete unknown work.
This lock governs Runtime canonical history/execution, not arbitrary trusted direct repository
administration; independent metadata controls such as source memory mode remain atomic DB operations.

Native local default sources re-read in full for archive_thread.rs and unarchive_thread.rs,
plus live_writer.rs create/resume and app-server thread_processor.rs1000–1085,1658–1755,

waits for shutdown and clears request/subscription/watch state. thread_lifecycle.rs414 wraps
shutdown_and_wait with10s timeout; on timeout the host proceeds, but the storage layer still

experimental behavior as the local default. Explicit include_archived resume exists in native

### Following environment/managed-layer boundary audit (no170 edits)

Native e80a50/579425/b49827 further distinguish source catalog from execution environment. In
codex-mcp/runtime::McpRuntimeContext, selected concrete environment handles are pinned first and the
canonical environment registry is fallback. Unknown nonlocal id fails startup; local HTTP alone may
use ambient HTTP without a registered environment. make_rmcp_client resolves this before transport:
local stdio uses LocalStdioServerLauncher, remote stdio uses ExecutorStdioServerLauncher from the
resolved exec backend; HTTP uses selected environment capability. Executor-owned bearer env vars are
resolved by executor only when http_header_env_vars capability permits, otherwise the native local
token-resolution path is explicit. Local HTTP header helpers reject nonlocal environment. This is
separate from catalog's pre-winner attachment authority (Pending/Failed/SelectedPluginsOnly/Restricted).

Corki config/features currently consumes environment_id only to reject nonlocal HTTP helpers, otherwise
does not retain it; client.create_client chooses only stdio/http and all environment resolution is local.
Thus adding an environment authority enum without retaining executor identity/routing would not align
the harness and could silently run a requested nonlocal command locally. Future work must distinguish
known local, unavailable/unknown and an explicitly host-bound executor, with its actual transport and
credential ownership. No remote executor transport implementation or live remote authority is claimed
by169. Native system requirements loader also distinguishes NotFound from fatal read errors and accepts
an explicit host override path; Corki CLI/config still has no managed-layer loader. These remain concrete
B/E dependencies rather than permission inferred from raw names, env values or model-generated metadata.

### Native executor follow-up evidence captured while172 gates run

exec-server/src/client/rpc_http_client.rs (69ae66): http_request_stream registers the route before
issuing http/request; it replaces caller stream IDs with monotonically allocated connection IDs
and uses a256-frame per-stream queue. Cancellation before headers removes the registration.
http_response_body_stream.rs (69ae66,8cc2bc) validates1-based sequence,1MiB decoded/encoded frame
limits and a shared16MiB queued-byte budget. Overflow removes only that stream and records a
failure; it must not block all other RPC traffic. Unknown/late IDs are ignored. Terminal errors,
disconnects and dropped streams remove routes/wake consumers; request IDs are not reused.
protocol.rs (28885a,d59e33) has ordered duplicate headers, optional valueEnvVar, bodyBase64,
timeoutMs(null/omitted disables), redirectPolicy and streamResponse; body notifications carry
requestId/seq/deltaBase64/done/error. rpc.rs (fc3709) uses Codex JSON-RPC envelopes WITHOUT a
jsonrpc field, string or i64 IDs, duplicate-key rejection and256K value-node limit. This cannot be
replaced blindly with the MCP JSON-RPC client. client.rs initialize_rpc (ee7625) sends clientName/
resumeSessionId, checks resumed session identity and emits initialized (not MCP initialized).
client_transport.rs (8cc2bc,ef7d7f) supports WebSocketUrl, NoiseRendezvous and StdioCommand;
connection.rs bounds stdio RPC frames at64MiB. Corki currently has no exec-server RPC module.
Next concrete step must implement the native HTTP RPC carrier under the now-working bound Runtime
path, not keep adding guard-only tests or pretend a supplied httpx carrier implements that protocol.

rmcp-client/src/http_client_adapter.rs (0ca64e): POST and common GET use streamed executor
requests; DELETE uses buffered HTTP. Initialization/discovery pass a remaining millisecond deadline,
ordinary requests/GET/DELETE leave executor timeout absent while outer request ownership controls
deadlines. Preserve explicit stop/follow redirect policy and repeated UTF-8 header values. A generic
httpx timeout dictionary must not silently become a different executor total-request deadline.

test126, cancelled-header request419, dropped consumer553, disconnect709, oversized delta779,

The full-queue tests deliberately send deltas before returning HTTP headers; a reader that awaits

### Next confirmed gap: MCP same-origin redirects (not yet implemented)

Source evidence d44b06/32bb4a/c2d840/884517: rmcp-client/http_client_adapter.rs:195 always stops
server/discover redirects; :772 stops protocol2026-07-28 and authenticated/configured AgentPluginV1
requests. Ordinary legacy requests follow, even with configured headers. codex-mcp/rmcp_client.rs
selects the mode from EffectiveMcpServer::is_agent_plugin, not a model- or server-supplied flag.
SameOriginRedirectHttpClient wraps all adapter HTTP carriers, forces each underlying hop to Stop,
and validates Location against the original origin before sending sensitive headers or a tool body.
It rejects plaintext non-localhost DNS redirects, limits hops to10 and shares the original deadline;
301/302 POST and303 switch to a bodyless GET (HEAD stays HEAD),307/308 retain method/body.
Content headers, proxy authorization and sanitized referer follow the native rules; each abandoned
stream must be dropped before the next hop. The helper's plaintext proxy-credential rejection is
an additional inner-carrier rule, not permission to silently strip helper headers and follow.

Corki currently sends follow_redirects=False in buffered_request, common GET and SSE reconnect,
and has no equivalent source/protocol-aware redirect layer. Real Runtime reproduction d3cf81:
the baseline bound carrier initializes and lists tools; adding a same-origin HTTPS307 to /final
produces a manager startup warning, zero handshakes and no request to /final. Thus this is a
confirmed B05/E transport availability mismatch, not a hypothetical missing feature. A safe fix
must cover POST/GET/DELETE and resumed streams, local/bound/executor carriers, exact source-mode
policy, deadlines, helper placement and no cross-origin request. Do not enable blind HTTPX redirects.
This audit does not alter frozen B code or claim the redirect gap closed; all A/C/D/E work remains.
